how: A member proposes participation and identifies a plot that another member then starts working on.
Calls recruit participants to make a national flag and supply a concrete plot and plan.
A coordinate-bearing call receives the bare affirmative answer Yalla.
Participants choose their national flag as the shared mark.
Participants dispute whether the available plot will make their flag large and visible enough.
Repeated coordinates and a red-line task make the plot findable enough for a participant to report starting.
A later call circulates coordinates and a linked plan described as vertical.
A participant explicitly reports finding the plot and beginning work.
Participants report the flag nearly done and subsequently claim completion.
Shared coordinates do not guarantee that an enthusiastic mobile participant can locate the flag.
A mobile locating difficulty warrants an access limitation rather than evidence of timer workarounds, scripts, bots or spare accounts.
The mobile difficulty supplies no observation of automated placement.
Task instructions and acceptance show practical coordination but cannot establish whether the room decided formal offices, voting rules or sanctions.
Selecting usable space includes arguing visibility and rejecting a location reportedly erased by other occupants.
After a proposed location is rejected because of reported deletion, the exchange returns to locating an available plot and specifying its red line.
Attribution is limited to one participant naming rainbow people as deleters, while a later warning leaves the damaging actor unknown.
A participant attributes deletion at a proposed location to rainbow people without showing any investigation.
A warning that someone is ruining the nearly completed flag supplies minimal watchfulness during building.
A warning during construction does not establish actual repairs, sustained defence or a separate post-completion upkeep stage.
A neighbouring national room asks for help and later reports success with thanks after another participant checks the result.
A request followed by success and thanks establishes acknowledged assistance but does not identify helpers or prove that their pixels caused completion.
A participant identifying with another room carries its flag-help appeal into the host thread.
The help appeal and thanks do not show any negotiated border, truce or bargain.
A proposed takeover is recorded without a coded refusal, restraint or apology.
Regional thanks do not establish a coalition, shared chat or mutual defence agreement.
Neither the plot instructions nor the help request establish a host granting permission over its own territory.
No dispute over authority to bind placers is evidenced in the help-request exchange.
Regional identification appears in thanks but cannot be treated as the demonstrated cause of help or as a broader national political argument.
A participant explicitly frames successful flag work and thanks through regional belonging by saying GCC for life.
The takeover suggestion supplies no evidence of a quarrel carried from before the canvas.
Saying other flags are too numerous does not establish that a prior rivalry or ideology selected the target.
Flag-building calls provide no evidence that a local April Fools prank framed their reception.
Calls to build are visible but no coded response regulates canvas discussion in the host room.
A collective completion claim marks the flag as an accomplishment.
An after-close question and affirmative answer record the fate of the requested neighbouring flag.
Regional thanks after closure do not propose a continuing joint project or another canvas.
The after-close exchange confirms an outcome without contesting a cleaned image or an account of the event.
A participant proposes taking over another flag because its kind already has too many instances.
The takeover proposal is the evidenced lower-range attack call and does not demonstrate that any takeover occurred.
A complaint about another room hogging hearts is local hostile commentary rather than demonstrated reciprocal contest with that room.
The complaint and takeover proposal show no ensuing exchange with a rival room.

statement: noticing and appreciating another canvas picture
how: A participant briefly notices and appreciates another game picture.
A bare correction to r/place repairs the shared venue reference without teaching canvas mechanics or carrying on unrelated ordinary conversation.
The opaque MOI call cannot establish which picture or reference the participant is identifying.
An opening proposal receives explicit agreement and a call to find a spot and begin.
A specific request to work on the red line receives a report that the respondent found it and started.
The call receives a bare affirmative reply, supporting the observed acceptance pair without testing preference for acceptance over refusal.
Watchfulness accompanies an almost-complete mark, but the exchange cannot establish that building caused repair or that a separate upkeep stage followed completion.
The damage warning supplies no account linking watchfulness to a negotiation with neighbours.
The coded takeover proposal supplies no settled border whose effect on restraint can be tested.
The damage warning supplies no evidence that strain led anyone to automated placement.
Progress and celebration occur in order but their separate speakers do not explain what caused the celebration.
Celebration precedes an after-close report about another flag without an explicit link between the two.
The after-close report supplies no decision to carry the effort into another purpose.
A visibility objection and rejection of a location do not establish too few hands causing a relocation.
Coordinates follow design and location talk but the linked plan cannot demonstrate a pixel-level template settling agreed design.
A damage warning precedes an incoming help appeal without evidence that local strain caused that appeal.
The incoming appeal supplies no account of a border deal opening a channel for help.
A takeover suggestion follows recruitment but does not say recruitment prompted the proposed attack.
The takeover proposal has no coded reply refusing it or explaining restraint.
The takeover proposal has no coded reply invoking a truce or offering a deal.
A complaint about hearts precedes a takeover proposal about other flags and cannot establish an ensuing contest with one rival.
The damage warning and regional thanks do not establish a coalition formed because of shared attack.
The recorded calls do not establish that a canvas flood caused host-room regulation.
A help request without an evidenced agreement supplies no test of an ensuing dispute over who may bind the room.
Concern about visibility does not establish that the room judged its hands insufficient or the canvas too full.
Rejecting one proposed location and later posting different coordinates does not establish a room relocation after its work was overrun.
